system_description.narrative_title: A Fractured, Multi‑Crisis Global Order: Energy, Finance, Tech, and War
system_description.narrative_summary: The international system is an open, tightly coupled process in flux where regional kinetic conflicts and maritime chokepoint attacks are provoking global energy shocks that amplify inflation and force tighter monetary policy. That financial stress — rising bond yields and market volatility — interacts with a simultaneous political and technological scramble over AI governance and strategic tech, all under the shadow of great‑power competition and disruptive domestic politics. These overlapping dynamics feed back into one another, increasing systemic sensitivity and raising the risk of spillovers across regions and markets.
system_description.scope: Nation‑states, regional blocs and alliances, major international institutions (central banks, IMF, UN, EU, NATO), global commodity and capital markets (oil, LNG, bonds), leading technology firms and AI development ecosystems, and ongoing regional conflicts (Middle East, Russia‑Ukraine, proxy wars).
system_description.super_system: The global political‑economic‑security system (planetary socio‑technical and economic order).

variables.name: Russia–Ukraine kinetic escalation
variables.description: Russia and Ukraine’s prolonged war is escalating with intensified drone and cross-border strikes that are raising NATO border incidents and shifting military postures in Eastern Europe.

variables.name: Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz disruptions
variables.description: Iran-backed Houthi operations and Gulf state countermeasures are turning the Red Sea and Strait of Hormuz into persistent maritime chokepoints that are disrupting oil shipments and regional security dynamics.

variables.name: U.S.–China high-tech and AI competition
variables.description: The United States and China are locked in a strategic rivalry over semiconductors, artificial intelligence governance and export controls as both sides tighten rules and race for technological leadership.

variables.name: Global monetary and market stress
variables.description: A rapid rise in interest rates and sovereign yields led by U.S. Fed tightening and inflation shocks is reshaping capital flows, lifting global borrowing costs and inflicting volatility across asset markets.

variables.name: BRICS geoeconomic realignment
variables.description: China, Russia, India and other BRICS states are deepening payments, trade and institutional links to build alternatives to Western-dominated economic governance and expand south–south cooperation.
